title: API rapid recovery checklist and triage notes (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, actionable runbook draft to assist first responders when we see API degradations: timeouts (client-visible), spikes in 429s (rate limiting), degraded streaming (stuttering or truncated streams), or sudden elevated error rates (5xx).

Audience and intent:
- Primary: on-call SRE doing first 15–30m triage.
- Secondary: devs and infra owners for escalation.
- Keep it short; use links to longer docs for follow-up.

Quick triage checklist (first 3 minutes)
1) Confirm alert & scope
   - Which alert fired: p95-latency, request-error-rate, 429-rate, streaming-drop-rate?
   - Scope: single route, model, region, or global? Check Alert details and Affected Routes on the Pager alert.
   - Slack channel: #sre-oncall and the route-specific channel (e.g. #api-gateway).

2) Basic telemetry to open immediately
   - Grafana: "API - Gateway Latency" (p50/p95/p99), "API - Error Breakdown" (4xx/5xx/429), "Serving Runtime - Tail Latency"
   - Datadog/Logs: search for repeated stack traces or 429 response patterns across nodes
   - Kinesis/Streaming metrics: "stream-chunk-drop-rate" for streaming failures

3) Rapid cause classification (pick best match)
   - Traffic surge (legit or bot): concurrent connections and per-route QPS increased by >2x
   - Capacity exhaustion at gateway or runtime (CPU/GPU saturation, queue length rising)
   - Downstream dependency failure (model health, KV cache, auth service)
   - Policy/bug causing excessive 429s (token bucket misconfig, new rate-limiter rule)
   - Regression in streaming code path (recent deploy)

Commands & quick probes (run on any responder laptop with credentials)
- Check ingress LB and API gateway health: kubectl -n gateway get pods -o wide --show-labels; kubectl logs <pod> -c envoy --since=2m | grep -i "429"
- Verify route-specific 429s from API: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <oncall-token>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?route=<affected>" |& sed -n '1,120p'
- Check model-serving pods: kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-<name> ; for pod in $(kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-<name> -o name); do kubectl -n serving top pod ${pod##*/}; done
- Streaming probe (quick): run the sample client against the affected stream route to reproduce partial/late chunks; capture timestamps

Immediate mitigation actions (pick and apply in order of least risk)
A) If 429s are spiky and tied to a misconfigured rate limiter:
   - Rollback recently applied rate-limiter config (ConfigMap / envoy filter).
   - Temporarily widen token bucket for affected routes: increase burst and refill_rate in feature flag.
   - If rate-limit is external (WAF/CDN), open a ticket with infra and patch via emergency config.

B) If latency/timeouts are due to runtime CPU/GPU saturation:
   - Scale serving deployment: kubectl -n serving scale deployment/model-<name> --replicas=<n+2> (watch for GPU quota limits).
   - If Dedicated pools are full, failover traffic to a compatible hosted model variant (policy: route -> model-variant-fallback).
   - Reduce per-request work: set max_tokens lower via header override for incoming traffic (API has header X-Override-MaxTokens).

C) If streaming degraded (stuttering/truncation):
   - Check network ECC/drop counters on nodes (SRE infra dashboard).
   - Toggle streaming mode to chunked-polling fallback where supported (feature flag) to keep UX while root cause is investigated.
   - If a recent code deploy touched streaming path, trigger a canary rollback for that service.

D) If errors (5xx) spike due to dependency (cache/db/auth):
   - Circuit-break dependent calls via runtime feature flags (short term).
   - Route small percentage of traffic to a cached static response for non-critical routes.

E) System-level stop-gap:
   - Global throttling: enforce stricter per-IP burst limits on CDN for a short window to protect backend.
   - Open incident bridge if impact > 5% of traffic or high-severity customers are affected.

Observability checks to run in parallel (delegable)
- Log sampling: tail the access logs for the affected route and grep for correlation-id patterns.
- CPU/GPU telemetry: check p95 GPU util and memory usage; look for OOM or worker restarts.
- Queue lengths: internal request queue depth > threshold? (service_queue_depth gauge)
- Rate-limiter metrics: token_bucket_dropped_count grouped by route

Escalation matrix
- If you cannot bring errors under target (error rate < 0.5% sustained in 15m): escalate to serving-runtime on-call (pager: SERVE_RUNTIME).
- If issue is cross-region or infra (LB/Cloud provider): escalate to platform-engineering on-call.
- If customer-impacting SLAs are violated: page SRE lead + Product Ops.

Communication guidance
- Post a short status in #sre-oncall and #incidents: what happened, who is on it, user impact (percent requests affected), mitigation in progress.
- Update incident bridge notes every 15 minutes during active remediation.

Post-incident: immediate postmortem checklist
- Capture timeline with exact times for alert, mitigation start, root cause and full recovery.
- Attach all relevant graphs (p50/p95 latency, 429/sec, error-rate) and logs.
- Identify concrete action items (e.g., change default rate limiter, add auto-scale rule for model-<name>, harden streaming buffer).
- Assign owners and ETA for each follow-up.

Root-cause hypotheses (common patterns we've seen)
- Bad rollout of a rate-limiter rule that applied globally instead of per-route.
- A/B experiment that increased per-request tokens causing GPU memory pressure.
- Cache eviction storm when many jobs miss a recently-warmed KV cache at midnight.
- Network path MTU changes causing chunked data reassembly issues for streaming.

Open questions / TODOs for this draft
- Define numeric thresholds: exact p95/p99 latency and error-rate thresholds per-product tranche.
- Add playbook for multi-region failover (runbooks currently assume single-region).
- Automate selective rollback: can we add a one-click rollback in console for recent envoy/filter changes?

Appendix: useful links and commands
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ApiGateway/api-gateway-overview
- Logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/queries?query=route:<placeholder>
- Common commands: kubectl -n serving get hpa; kubectl -n gateway logs -l app=gateway -c envoy --tail=200
- Runbook canonical: CONFLUENCE-API-RUNBOOK-123 (long form)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc short. Move long checks to the canonical runbook but retain a one-page cheat for oncall.
- Add a short checklist card to the oncall rotation playbook for monthly drills.
- Worth running a synthetic that intentionally triggers burst 429s to exercise mitigation paths.

End of draft.
